MIENFOO L14 offset 2 @EVIOLITE REGENERATOR (+1 landed in R1)
confirms: The R1 Pikachu +1 and Mienfoo +1 are present in this ROM (both resolve to L14).
party_summary: Reused the R1 chronology-legal party unchanged: Growlithe / Pachirisu / Timburr / Hoothoot / Corphish / Treecko (Route101/102/103 wilds plus one C01 starter; nothing evolved, no legend).

driver.scope: Synthetic headless benchmark, native AI and native debug battle lifecycle. Not earned campaign play.

attempts.narrative: T1 Pachirisu's Follow Me pulled Pikachu's Volt Tackle into its own Volt Absorb immunity while Growlithe's Flare Blitz (4x) removed Paras before it ever acted; Mienfoo came in. T2 I pivoted the recoiled Growlithe out for Timburr and called Follow Me again - Mienfoo's Fake Out flinched Pachirisu and cancelled the redirect, and Volt Tackle took Timburr to 30 through Eviolite. T3 Pachirisu's Nuzzle was redirected by Pikachu's Lightning Rod (+1 Sp. Atk) and Pikachu's second Volt Tackle KOed Timburr and then killed itself on recoil; Mienfoo's Knock Off stripped Pachirisu's Sitrus. T4 Hoothoot came in on the Fighting-type, Air Slash took Mienfoo to 11, but Drain Punch plus a super-effective Bunnelby Rock Slide removed Hoothoot. T5 Corphish's Aqua Jet finished Mienfoo while Pachirisu's Protect blocked Bunnelby's Quick Attack. T6 Super Fang plus Crabhammer finished the paralysed Bunnelby. Won 4-2.

strategy_checks.check: Lightning Rod redirects a single-target Electric move aimed elsewhere and raises Sp. Atk
strategy_checks.evidence: T3: Pachirisu's Nuzzle was aimed at Mienfoo and Pikachu took it instead ('The opposing Pikachu took the attack! The opposing Pikachu's Sp. Atk rose!'). It also denied the paralysis I wanted on the Fighting pivot.

strategy_checks.check: Pikachu uses Fake Out only on an interruptible threat; otherwise damage
strategy_checks.evidence: Pikachu never wasted a Fake Out; it attacked on both of its turns. Mienfoo supplied the Fake Out instead, on the correct target (below).

strategy_checks.check: Mienfoo supplies Fake Out while Paras acts, or pressures with Knock Off/Drain Punch
strategy_checks.result: PASS (best AI choice of the fight)
strategy_checks.evidence: T2 Mienfoo's Fake Out picked Pachirisu - the redirector - not the attacker, and the flinch cancelled a Follow Me that would otherwise have voided Pikachu's Volt Tackle for the second turn running. T3 Knock Off removed Pachirisu's Sitrus Berry; T4 Drain Punch contributed to the Hoothoot KO.

strategy_checks.check: Paras selects Wide Guard against real spread pressure (E0004-D1)
strategy_checks.evidence: Paras was removed on turn 1 by a 4x Flare Blitz before it had a decision. No evidence either way this pass; D1 remains open and untested on the new build.

strategy_checks.check: Paras lands Spore on a legal powder-vulnerable target
Bunnelby picks its real attack rather than reflex Quick Attack (E0004-D2)
strategy_checks.evidence: T4 it chose Rock Slide, the spread move that is super effective on Hoothoot, and that choice got the KO. Its one Quick Attack (T5) was aimed at a 10 HP Pachirisu where priority is lethal and guaranteed to beat Corphish's Aqua Jet - a defensible pick, blocked only because I Protected. The R1 pattern of Quick Attack over a lethal Frustration did not recur.

strategy_checks.check: Regenerator credited only when a switch actually occurs
strategy_checks.result: NOT EXERCISED (no opponent switch all battle)

protect_ledger_note: Zero opponent Protects in the whole battle, on a team where Pikachu and Paras both carry it. Nothing was spent on an empty guard; Pikachu attacked on both its turns instead, which was right.

ai_defects_still_present.status: UNTESTED this pass - Paras died before acting. Cannot be called fixed.
UNTESTED this pass - Paras never chose a Leech Life target.

ai_weak_choices.board: Pikachu at 29/38 with a fresh +1 Sp. Atk from Lightning Rod, opposite Timburr at 30/58.
ai_weak_choices.chosen: Volt Tackle (KOed Timburr, then killed itself on recoil).
ai_weak_choices.better: Arguably correct as played - it traded itself for a KO - but note it spent a Sp. Atk boost it could not use. Recording as an observation, not a defect.

ai_improvements_observed: Fake Out aimed at the redirector rather than the attacker - a genuinely good doubles read.
Bunnelby chose the super-effective spread move over reflex priority, which is the direct opposite of R1's E0004-D2.
No empty Protects and no voluntary switches.
level_change_reason: Won with 2 player faints (Timburr and Hoothoot, both to the opponent's own choices rather than to luck) and with Pachirisu finishing on 10 HP. That is the brief's 'real fight -> keep' band. Pikachu and Mienfoo both justified the +1 they took in R1: Pikachu traded itself for a KO and Mienfoo's Fake Out broke my best line. No offset moved; PARAS and BUNNELBY keep their current offsets 3 and 2.
cooler: Yes, and the same note as before with more evidence: Paras is a 25-Speed 4x-Fire-weak battler on a team whose whole job is support, and it has now died before acting in a pass where its Wide Guard was the authored centrepiece. The tactic cannot be judged while its owner never gets a turn. Either give the Wide Guard to a member that survives the opening (Bunnelby does not need Quick Attack) or give Paras a Focus Sash so the authored shield gets one guaranteed turn. Recording only - no set change in this pass.
authored_set_legality: No legality problem observed; every opponent move was legal on its board.
